extracted.intended_audience: clinical researchers, psychometricians, instrument developers, and clinicians conducting reliability/validity studies of assessment tools
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and reporting reliability and validity of clinical assessment instruments (inter-rater, intra-rater, internal consistency, test-retest, and various validity types) across health and rehabilitation settings. Includes practical guidance on training, translation/adaptation, and choice of agreement statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-rater reliability (Kappa)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter-rater agreement assessed with Cohen's Kappa (including unweighted and weighted variants) reported for items and domains; example thresholds used: Kappa > 0.7 = good/substantial, 0.5-0.7 = fair/moderate, < 0.5 = poor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report kappa values for individual items and domains, and summarize proportions of items meeting thresholds (e.g., percent of items with Kappa>0.7). Use linear or quadratic weighting for ordinal scales when appropriate. Provide 95% confidence intervals when possible. Interpret kappa in context (percent agreement may be high even when kappa is low).

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of internal consistency of scale dimensions using Cronbach's alpha; values > 0.7 generally considered substantial/good, lower values indicate poor internal consistency (example: one dimension had alpha = 0.375).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report alpha for each dimension/subscale. If alpha is low, examine item heterogeneity and consider removing/modifying items or re-evaluating dimensionality (factor analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted kappa (linear and quadratic) for ordinal data
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of linear weighted kappa and quadratic weighted kappa to summarize agreement on ordinal scales (e.g., overall scores or categories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose weighting appropriate to the ordinal structure (linear or quadratic). Be aware of paradoxical properties of the quadratically weighted kappa (e.g., counterintuitive behavior for odd-numbered category tables) and report which weighting was used. Supplement with percent agreement and other metrics as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) for summary scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ICC to assess inter-rater (and intra-rater) reliability of total/summary scores or continuous measures (examples: ICC = 0.97 for scale sum score).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify ICC model and form (e.g., ICC(2,1) vs ICC(3,k)), report 95% confidence intervals, and interpret magnitude (e.g., values near 1 indicate excellent agreement). Use ICC for continuous/interval/ratio aggregate scores rather than item-level categorical data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test–retest reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Stability of measurements across time assessed by re-administration or repeated observation (measured with percent agreement, kappa, correlations, ICC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report retest interval, metrics (kappa, correlation coefficients, ICC), and confidence intervals. Evaluate whether temporal stability is appropriate for construct being measured and ensure conditions between administrations are comparable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intra-rater reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistency of the same rater's assessments across occasions, quantified with kappa, ICC, or correlation coefficients (examples: intrarater kappa/ICC ranges reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use video or repeated live assessments to estimate intra-rater consistency, specify time between ratings, and report reliability statistics with CIs. If low, consider additional rater training or clarifying item definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple proportion of exact agreement between raters reported alongside kappa statistics (examples: overall percent agreement reported e.g., 85% agreement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present percent agreement together with chance-corrected measures (kappa) because percent agreement does not account for agreement expected by chance. Use when interpretability of kappa is problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of correlation coefficients (Spearman, Pearson) for reliability/validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Spearman rank correlation and Pearson product-moment correlation used to assess associations for reliability (and criterion/concurrent validity) between ratings, scores, or instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose Spearman for ordinal/non-normal data and Pearson for continuous/normal data. Report correlation coefficients, sample sizes, and significance; interpret strength in context and supplement with agreement measures when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity assessments: face, content, construct, criterion-related/concurrent validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate validity through expert review (face/content), construct validation (known-group differences, expected correlations), and criterion/concurrent validity by comparison to reference/gold-standard instruments (use AUC, sensitivity, specificity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document procedures for establishing face and content validity (expert panels). For concurrent/criterion validity, administer comparator instruments (e.g., K-SADS-PL) and report AUC, sensitivity, specificity, and kappa for diagnostic concordance. When comparable measures are lacking, state limitations on criterion validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison to gold-standard/reference instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Concordance and diagnostic agreement assessed by comparing new/short instruments to established reference tools (examples: MINI-KID vs K-SADS-PL; EDACS vs BODS/MACS/WeeFIM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use masked/blinded assessment and counterbalanced administration on the same day where feasible. Report AUC, kappa, sensitivity, specificity, and differences in time-to-administer. Discuss trade-offs between brevity and diagnostic accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rater training, retraining, and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of structured training (including retraining and certification) to raters to improve inter- and intra-rater reliability (examples: in-depth training and certification for ISAT; training/retraining improved infant arousal scoring reliability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe training content, duration, practice and calibration sessions, and whether raters were certified. Report pre- and post-training reliability to demonstrate impact. Use standardized materials (manuals, videos) and consensus discussions to resolve discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation and cross-cultural adaptation procedures (TCCA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal multi-step translation and cross-cultural adaptation procedures applied when adapting instruments to other languages/cultures (example: nine-step TCCA for ABS-G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document forward/back translation, expert committee review, pretesting/pilot, and cultural adaptation steps. After translation, re-evaluate psychometrics (inter/intra-rater reliability, internal consistency, validity) in target population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode of observation: real-time vs video ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment method (live real-time observation vs video-recorded ratings) affects reliability; some studies reported low agreement between real-time and video (example: real-time vs video ICC = 0.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report mode used and, if both used, compare agreement. Acknowledge potential validity limitations of video recordings and document procedures for capturing equivalent vantage points and audio/visual quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item-level versus summary-score reliability and item modification
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability should be reported at the item level and for summary scores; some items/components may show variable agreement and warrant modification (studies recommend modifying criteria where excellence was not reached).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide item-level kappa/ICC ranges, identify poorly performing items, and consider revising item definitions, response categories, or scoring instructions. Reassess psychometrics after modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting confidence intervals and sample/context details
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide 95% confidence intervals for kappa/ICC and describe sample characteristics, rater backgrounds, assessment settings, and retest intervals (examples: kappa with 95% CI reported for NOT-S linear weighted kappa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include CIs to convey precision of estimates. Report sample size, subject demographics, rater experience, and context (e.g., inpatient vs community) to aid generalizability judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety, feasibility, and clinical relevance of operational definitions/tests
rubrics_metrics.description: When instruments involve physiological testing or clinical protocols (e.g., physiologic definition of BPD using oxygen saturation monitoring), evaluate safety, feasibility, inter-rater reliability, test-retest reliability, and correlation with clinical outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor and report adverse events (e.g., apnea, bradycardia), feasibility metrics, and associations with meaningful outcomes (discharge on oxygen, length of stay, readmissions). A reliable instrument should also be safe and clinically useful in trials.
